Each row in the discussions list now shows how many comments the discussion has and when the last one was written, or "No comments yet". As you asked, I didn't run tests, lint or the app, so none of this has been checked by running it. The project's rule-check hook raised no issues on the final version of the files I changed.

**What changed**

- **Mock API** (`src/testing/mocks/handlers/discussions.ts`): `GET /discussions` now returns `commentsCount` and `lastCommentAt` with each discussion. `lastCommentAt` is the time of the newest comment, or `null` when there are none.
- **Types** (`features/discussions/api/get-discussions.ts`): I added a `DiscussionListItem` type with the two new fields. I put it here instead of in `src/types/api.ts` because that file says it is auto-generated.
- **List** (`features/discussions/components/discussions-list.tsx`): two new columns, "Comments" and "Last Comment".

**Keeping the counts current**

The app keeps query results cached for 60 seconds. Without a fix, the list would show old counts right after someone adds or deletes a comment. So I added a `useInvalidateDiscussions` hook to the same API file. The discussion page (`app/routes/app/discussions/discussion.tsx`) calls it when you leave the page, and the list then fetches fresh data. Comments can only be added or deleted on that page.

My first try was to refresh the list from the comment hooks themselves. The rule-check hook blocked that, because features can't import each other and query keys can't be written by hand. Calling the query client straight from the route was also blocked, which is why the refresh now lives in the discussions API file. I removed those first attempts, so nothing from them is left in the code.
